$comment: Test fixture exercising all fields of the EU Succession extension schema

europeanCertificate.issuingAuthority: Tribunal judiciaire de Paris, Pôle Successions

spanishRegionalRegime.forcedHeirshipRules: Catalan Civil Code Book IV — legitimate portion (llegítima) is 25% of estate divided equally among descendants
spanishRegionalRegime.notes: Applicable to immovable property situated in Catalonia. The deceased held a holiday villa in Girona subject to Catalan forced heirship rules despite habitual residence in France.

forcedHeirshipVariant.claimNature: Réserve héréditaire — real right in the estate, not merely a monetary claim
forcedHeirshipVariant.calculationNotes: Two surviving children: reserved portion is 2/3 of the net estate (Code civil Art. 913). The disposable portion (quotité disponible) is 1/3.
forcedHeirshipVariant.reformVersion: Law 2006-728 of 23 June 2006 reforming successions and gifts

temporalRule.legislativeReference: Code civil Art. 913 (as amended by Law 2006-728)
temporalRule.notes: The 2006 reform reduced the reserved portion for two children from 3/4 to 2/3 and introduced the renunciation anticipée (advance waiver).

postBrexitHandling.ukAssetsHandledUnder: English domestic law — UK is not bound by Brussels IV Regulation post-Brexit
postBrexitHandling.notes: The deceased held a buy-to-let flat in London. As the UK does not participate in Brussels IV, English succession law applies to the UK-situs immovable property. A separate English grant of probate is required.

legislativeChanges.description: European Commission review of Brussels IV Regulation (EU) No 650/2012 — proposed amendments to strengthen mutual recognition of authentic instruments
legislativeChanges.notes: Public consultation closed February 2026. Draft amendments expected Q3 2026. Focus on reducing refusal grounds for recognition of ECS across member states.

legislativeChanges.description: French Cour de cassation ruling (Civ. 1re, 15 March 2025) confirming that Brussels IV choice-of-law election survives a subsequent change of habitual residence
legislativeChanges.notes: Landmark ruling clarifying that a valid nationality election under Article 22 of Brussels IV is not invalidated by later relocation to a different member state.

notes: Fictional estate of Marco Bianchi, Italian national habitually resident in Paris, deceased 10 July 2025. Cross-border estate spanning France, Italy (nationality election), Spain (Catalan property), and England (post-Brexit investment property). Two surviving children entitled to French réserve héréditaire.
